claims.text: A 50–100 nm TiN interlayer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the TiN interlayer will prevent premature coating failure in high-temperature steam.
The TiN interlayer will preserve the Cr coating's corrosion resistance during normal subcritical-water operation.
Normal PWR subcritical-water operation is represented by temperatures of approximately 300–400°C.
Accident-relevant exposure is represented by steam at up to approximately 800°C for about 30 minutes.
The proposed TiN layer is dense.
The proposed TiN layer is chemically inert at the Cr/zirconium-alloy interface.
The proposed TiN layer is thermally stable under the specified water and steam exposures.
TiN can function as a physical barrier to atomic diffusion.
TiN reduces Cr–Zr interdiffusion by presenting a high-energy diffusion barrier.
The TiN interlayer prevents formation of deleterious Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds.
Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds formed without the barrier would compromise coating adhesion.
Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds formed without the barrier would compromise oxidation resistance.
Suppressing interdiffusion will limit development of a degraded interfacial region during high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to direct Cr coating, the TiN-interlayered system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to direct Cr coating, the TiN-interlayered system will exhibit enhanced coating adhesion.
Relative to direct Cr coating, the TiN-interlayered system will sustain oxidation resistance under both normal-water and accident-steam conditions.
An elemental Cr coating applied directly to zirconium alloy is prone to premature failure because of elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
